boring_rival_explanations: Fitness level drives both ANS reactivity phenotype and SNR, not a distinct ANS trait
Medication effects masquerade as phenotype differences
Age-related vascular stiffening reduces PPG amplitude independent of ANS
confounder_rival_builds.rival_prediction: VO2max will explain more variance in per-subject SNR and detection uncertainty than the ANS_reactivity_phenotype_score; when VO2max is covaried, the phenotype score loses significant predictive power.
confounder_rival_builds.distinguishing_condition: In a hierarchical regression predicting per-subject ECE, adding VO2max in step 1 renders the ANS_reactivity_phenotype_score non-significant in step 2 (ΔR² < 0.01, p > 0.05), whereas the reverse order leaves VO2max significant.
confounder_rival_builds.confounder_rival_notes: Fitness is a known determinant of both baseline HRV and stress reactivity. Must measure VO2max directly (not estimated) and exclude medicated participants. Residualize phenotype score for fitness before testing.

possible_confounders: Sensor band tightness and placement consistency
boring_rival_explanations: Loose vs. tight band fit explains signal quality variation better than skin properties
Wrist size determines optical path length more than epidermal thickness
Movement artifacts correlate with hair density but are caused by activity, not hair
confounder_rival_builds.rival_prediction: Within-subject variation in band tightness (measured via force sensor) will predict PPG/EDA signal quality indices more strongly than between-subject skin property measures.
confounder_rival_builds.distinguishing_condition: A linear mixed model with random intercepts for subject shows band_tightness_N as a significant fixed effect (p < 0.001) on PPG SQI, while stratum_corneum_hydration_AU becomes non-significant (p > 0.1) when both are included.
confounder_rival_builds.confounder_rival_notes: Band tightness is rarely measured but critically affects contact. Use instrumented strap with force sensor. Standardize placement with 3D-printed guide. Measure skin temp via infrared to separate vascular from interface effects.

boring_rival_explanations: Homeostatic sleep pressure (prior wake duration) drives baseline autonomic shifts, not circadian phase
Caffeine's half-life creates time-of-day confounding with chronotype
Morning vs. evening activity patterns differ by chronotype and affect physiology
confounder_rival_builds.rival_prediction: Prior wake duration will predict resting RMSSD and stress reactivity at fixed clock times better than phase angle; controlling for wake duration eliminates the phase angle effect.
confounder_rival_builds.distinguishing_condition: In a mixed model with phase_angle_minutes and prior_wake_duration_h as predictors of baseline RMSSD, the coefficient for prior_wake_duration_h remains significant (p < 0.01) while phase_angle_minutes becomes non-significant (p > 0.1) when both are included.
confounder_rival_builds.confounder_rival_notes: Chronotype correlates with sleep timing. Use forced desynchrony or constant routine to truly isolate circadian phase. At minimum, measure and control prior wake duration via actigraphy. Caffeine logs essential.

possible_confounders: Seasonal variation in physiology and behavior
Wearable sensor firmware updates or drift
boring_rival_explanations: Sensor degradation or firmware changes create artificial drift mimicking habituation
Seasonal changes in temperature/light drive physiological trends
Life events (exams, holidays) cause non-stationarity unrelated to stressor repetition
confounder_rival_builds.rival_prediction: A control mannequin wearing the same device model will show similar feature drift over 28 days if sensor drift is the cause; human data will show additional subject-specific trajectories.
confounder_rival_builds.distinguishing_condition: Compare slope distributions of EDA_peak_frequency over deployment days between human participants (n≥30) and a mannequin control (n=5 devices). If human slopes are significantly more variable (Levene's test p < 0.01) and include both negative and positive slopes while mannequin slopes are near zero and unidirectional, habituation/sensitization is supported over sensor drift.
confounder_rival_builds.confounder_rival_notes: Deploy identical devices on mannequins in same environment. Log firmware updates. Use menstrual tracking apps. Exclude participants with major routine changes. Seasonal effect controlled by staggered enrollment or including day_of_year as spline.

possible_confounders: Stressor ambiguity (unclear whether event is stressful)
EMA prompt timing relative to stressor onset/offset
Cognitive load at time of prompt
boring_rival_explanations: Ambiguous stressors produce inconsistent labels regardless of subject traits
Prompts delivered during stressor recovery vs. peak create systematic misalignment
High cognitive load at prompt time impairs recall for all subjects equally
confounder_rival_builds.rival_prediction: Label noise (estimated via physiological consistency) will be higher for ambiguous stressors and mistimed prompts across all subjects, with trait scores (TAS-20, BFI-2) explaining minimal additional variance.
confounder_rival_builds.distinguishing_condition: A variance partitioning analysis (hierarchical regression) shows stressor_ambiguity_rating and prompt_stressor_latency_min jointly explain >40% of per-subject label_noise_estimate variance, while adding TAS20_alexithymia_score and BFI2_conscientiousness_score increases R² by <5% (ΔR² < 0.05, p > 0.05).
confounder_rival_builds.confounder_rival_notes: Stressor ambiguity rated by independent coders from EMA free-text. Prompt latency logged automatically. Use experience sampling with random prompts to decorrelate prompt timing from stressor timing. Validate label noise with structured interview subset.

possible_confounders: Stressor intensity and duration variation across contexts
Baseline physiological state at stressor onset
boring_rival_explanations: Social contexts involve more intense stressors, not distinct physiology
Physical threat contexts have longer duration, causing greater EDA
Predictability differences across contexts drive physiology, not context per se
confounder_rival_builds.rival_prediction: When stressor intensity, duration, and predictability are matched across contexts (via experimental manipulation or statistical control), context-specific physiological reactivity differences and detection performance disparities will disappear.
confounder_rival_builds.distinguishing_condition: In a lab study with orthogonally manipulated context (social vs. non-social) and stressor intensity (low vs. high), the context × intensity interaction on HRV_reactivity is non-significant (p > 0.1), while intensity main effect is significant (p < 0.001). Context-conditional models show no improvement over intensity-only models (ΔECE < 0.005).
confounder_rival_builds.confounder_rival_notes: Naturalistic data cannot fully disentangle context from stressor properties. Need experimental manipulation: same stressor type (e.g., cognitive task) in different contexts with intensity matched. Measure coping via brief post-stressor EMA. Control baseline with pre-stressor window.

boring_rival_explanations: Environmental temperature drives both motion (thermoregulation) and PPG noise
EMI from nearby electronics causes burst artifacts unrelated to subject traits
Device self-heating alters sensor characteristics over recording session
confounder_rival_builds.rival_prediction: Noise distribution parameters (kurtosis, burst rate) will correlate more strongly with concurrent environmental measures (ambient_temp_C, EMI_index) than with subject ID; within-subject noise varies more across environments than between subjects in the same environment.
confounder_rival_builds.distinguishing_condition: A variance components analysis (random effects model) shows environment (session-level) explains >50% of variance in motion_artifact_burst_rate and EDA_baseline_drift_volatility, while subject ID explains <20%. ICC for subject < 0.3.
confounder_rival_builds.confounder_rival_notes: Record environment continuously. Use Faraday cage for lab sessions to isolate EMI. Monitor device temp via internal sensor. Compare same subject across multiple days/environments. Trait-like noise requires high ICC across environments.

boring_rival_explanations: High interoceptive accuracy individuals attend more to bodily sensations during any stressor, amplifying physiology via attention, not coupling gain
Interoceptive stressors (e.g., CO2 challenge) inflate coupling for high IA; exteroceptive stressors (e.g., speech) do not
Anxiety sensitivity drives both IA questionnaire scores and physiological reactivity
confounder_rival_builds.rival_prediction: The coupling gain slope (physiology per VAS unit) will be significantly steeper for high IA individuals only during interoceptive-focused stressors; during exteroceptive stressors (e.g., Trier Social Stress Test), the IA × stressor interaction on coupling gain will be non-significant.
confounder_rival_builds.distinguishing_condition: In a within-subject design with counterbalanced interoceptive (cold pressor, CO2) and exteroceptive (TSST, mental arithmetic) stressors, the correlation between interoceptive_accuracy and coupling_gain_slope is significant (p < 0.01) for interoceptive stressors but not for exteroceptive stressors (p > 0.2), tested via Fisher's z-test for dependent correlations.
confounder_rival_builds.confounder_rival_notes: Must manipulate stressor modality. Control respiration (paced breathing) to isolate autonomic from respiratory effects. Measure anxiety sensitivity (ASI-3) as covariate. Use multiple IA measures (heartbeat counting, heartbeat discrimination, MAIA).

possible_confounders: Fixed epoch length mismatched to recovery dynamics
boring_rival_explanations: Fixed 1-min epochs are too long for fast recoverers (smearing) and too short for slow recoverers (fragmentation)
Longer stressors produce longer recovery, not trait-like recovery kinetics
Post-stressor movement accelerates recovery via mechanical artifact, not autonomic rebound
confounder_rival_builds.rival_prediction: Using adaptive epoch lengths (e.g., scaled to individual recovery half-life) will eliminate the correlation between recovery half-life and boundary misclassification rate; fixed epochs produce the correlation artifactually.
confounder_rival_builds.distinguishing_condition: Compute boundary misclassification rate using fixed 1-min epochs and using personalized epochs (length = 2 × subject's HRV_recovery_half_life). The correlation between HRV_recovery_half_life and misclassification rate is significant (p < 0.01) for fixed epochs but non-significant (p > 0.2) for personalized epochs.
confounder_rival_builds.confounder_rival_notes: Recovery half-life must be estimated independently (e.g., from separate recovery-only session). Control post-stressor activity strictly (seated). Exclude caffeine/nicotine. Test multiple epoch lengths. Compare fixed-window CNN vs. semi-Markov CRF with learned state durations.

boring_rival_explanations: Ancestry differences correlate with both genotype frequencies and autonomic physiology
Observed SNPs are proxies for unmeasured causal variants in LD
Genotype effects only appear under high stress exposure (G×E), not main effects
confounder_rival_builds.rival_prediction: The association between ADRB1/ADRB2/COMT genotypes and HRV/EDA reactivity will become non-significant after controlling for the first 10 genetic ancestry principal components; the mixture model bimodality will disappear in ancestry-homogeneous subsamples.
confounder_rival_builds.distinguishing_condition: In a linear mixed model predicting HRV_stress_reactivity with genotype as fixed effect and ancestry PCs as covariates, the genotype effect is non-significant (p > 0.05) while PCs are significant (p < 0.01). Mixture model BIC improvement over single Gaussian drops from >10 to <2 when analyzed within a single ancestry cluster (e.g., European PC1/PC2 cluster).
confounder_rival_builds.confounder_rival_notes: Population stratification is the primary rival for genetic associations. Must use homogeneous ancestry cohort (e.g., European only via PCs) or include PCs as covariates. Test G×E by adding stress_exposure × genotype interaction. Check LD structure. Exclude medicated participants. Power for minority homozygotes requires large N.
